facts.text: Casas Adobes means "adobe houses" in Spanish, reflecting the traditional building material used by early settlers.
Archaeological evidence shows human occupation in the Mimbres Valley dating back to the Archaic period, around 2000 B.C.
Mimbres artisans crafted black‑on‑white pottery with intricate animal and mythological designs, a hallmark of the region’s pre‑colonial culture.
In April 2020, the Grant County Commission officially designated the Casas Adobes subdivision as a colonia under U.S. HUD criteria.
New Mexico State Road 152 skirts just south of Casas Adobes, connecting the community westward to Santa Clara and eastward over the Black Range to Hillsboro.
New Mexico’s 1912 statehood settled long‑standing Spanish and Mexican land‑grant disputes in Grant County, paving the way for stable ranching and resource extraction.
